### LOW: Threat model does not cover the new default\-on encrypted SSD cache and full\-state codec for a GLM model
[docs/architecture/prefix\-cache\.md:149](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/f0ff572f5b03c94802d4ce58c276e7a472d64344/docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md#L149) · A-001, T-041

The new prefix\-cache\.md section says SSD eligibility defaults on for the locally selected EigenLabs/GLM\-5\.3\-Flash\-MLX\-NVFP4\-mtp \(PrefixCachePolicy\.isGLM5NextDefaultModel\)\. It also adds a distinct on\-disk layout, native\-paged\-glm5next\-full\-state\-v1, which stores sparse latent, index\-key, convolution/recurrence and MTP state\. T\-041 documents the SSD tier's at\-rest and TTFT\-oracle posture, its sign\-off and its affected\_files list, and none of these cover the new GLM codec or default\-on activation\. T\-041's cacheSalt scoping assumes a coordinator\-authored salt\. The doc says GLM is outside the registered coordinator serving models, so the supplied text does not show what tenant scope, TTL, per\-donation gating or KEK/HMAC lookup\-tag binding apply on the local path\. This is a documentation and threat\-model gap, not a demonstrated vulnerability\. Fix: add the GLM codec and policy files to T\-041, state the cacheSalt source in local mode, and confirm that HMAC lookup tags, the 30\-minute sliding TTL and the donation gates apply to the new layout\.

Raised by: anthropic/claude\-sonnet\-5\.5

### LOW: Debug cache\-KEK\-from\-file path is not reflected in the cache threat model
[docs/architecture/security/encryption\.md:113](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/f0ff572f5b03c94802d4ce58c276e7a472d64344/docs/architecture/security/encryption.md#L113) · A-001, T-041

The encryption doc now describes a DEBUG\-build path where the SSD cache KEK is derived from an operator\-created file \(\`DARKBLOOM\_DEBUG\_CACHE\_KEY\_FILE\`\)\. That file is protected only by ownership, mode 0600 and volume encryption, not the Secure Enclave\. T\-041 and its KEK\-wipe, HMAC\-lookup and at\-rest mitigations assume the KEK is rooted in the Secure Enclave\. A local process or operator that reads the file can decrypt DBK3 prompt\-derived KV artifacts and recompute the HMAC lookup keys, which undercuts the leak\-\#2 closure\. The doc says release builds do not contain this path, but the implementation \(\`SSDDebugCacheKeyFile\.swift\`\) is not in the supplied evidence, so that claim is unverified\. T\-041 and its detection hints should record this as a build\-gated weaker key\-custody mode\. A release\-build compile\-out check and a test that a release binary ignores the env var should also be required\.

Raised by: anthropic/claude\-sonnet\-5\.5
